subject: OptiLedger: concurrency decay and error wave after v3.1q deploy
messages:
From: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@optiledger.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Cc: OptiLedger Engineering <eng@optiledger.com>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:23:00 -0700
Subject: Re: v3.1q rollout - sudden P95/500s spike

Soojin, team —

We rolled the v3.1q quant profile at 03:00 PT this morning and started seeing issues within the hour. Summary from our telemetry (attached perf snapshot):
- P95 latency climbed from ~310ms -> 1.8s across our high-concurrency flows
- Error rate (5xx) increased to ~4.6% (baseline <0.2%)
- Overall throughput dropped ~28% despite routing more traffic to the instance pool

This is a production-impacting regression for our real-time document pipeline (high concurrency, short context). We put the service into a degraded routing policy but customers are experiencing timeouts. Attaching logs and a small traffic sample (optiledger-error-sample.tar.gz).

Can you confirm whether the v3.1q profile changed the KV cache layout or batching strategy? We need an ETA on a mitigation plan (rollback or patch). We're opening an internal incident on our side but this needs immediate attention and executive visibility if it won't be resolved within the next 3 hours.

Thanks —
Sandeep
Director, Platform Engineering
OptiLedger

Attachments: perf-snapshot-20270514.json, optiledger-error-sample.tar.gz

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@optiledger.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 09:42:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: v3.1q rollout - sudden P95/500s spike

Sandeep —

Thank you for the rapid heads-up and the artifacts. I’m escalating this to our engineering leadership and infra leads now. Initial notes from our side: the v3.1q profile enabled more aggressive token quantization for the attention kernels and adjusted the KV compression threshold — both intended to reduce memory and increase throughput but may regress hotpath latency at very high concurrency.

Immediate asks:
- Karthik, can you validate whether the deployed binary used the v3.1q runtime knobs (kernel selection + continuous batching) or if there was a mismatch with the canary config?
- Marissa, please stand by to coordinate a rollback if we advise it. We should draft a customer communication and a short credits/SLA mitigation proposal in case downtime extends.

Sandeep, I’ll ping back within 30 minutes with either a mitigation plan or an executive-level update. If we need to involve ops for an urgent rollback, I’ll include Jonas.

Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
mobile: +1-415-555-0126

[Attachment referenced: playbook-rollback-v3.1q.pdf — internal playbook for safe rollback procedures]

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 10:05:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: v3.1q rollout - sudden P95/500s spike

Looping in infra ops and assigning incident priority P0. Quick operational directives:
1) Snapshot the current serving pool (preserve KV caches) and capture perf traces (trace-id in related_links).
2) If Karthik confirms config drift or an incompatible quant path, prepare an immediate rollback to v3.0q canary (canary -> full rollback) — target < 30 minutes for the canary cut.
3) If rollback is not viable (stateful incompatibility), we will trigger a hotfix branch (low-risk change to batching window and KV threshold) and promote to canary.

Soojin: prepare an executive note for OptiLedger (what happened, impact window, next steps + compensation proposal). We should offer a temporary routing knob (route <10% of traffic to a low-latency fallback model) as a stopgap.

Jonas Weber
VP, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 11:10:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: v3.1q rollout - sudden P95/500s spike

Quick diagnostic from the canary logs attached in the Drive link:
- The deployed binary used the v3.1q knobs; however, one of the autoscale agents applied a higher concurrency setting to the burst pool that exposed a path in the attention kernel where quantized matmul falls back to an unoptimized path under contention. That increases tail latency dramatically.
- KV compression is working but the recompute penalty for short contexts added ~120-170ms per request under contention.

I recommend the following order of actions:
A) Immediate temporary mitigation (0-30m): flip routing to route 15% of traffic to the v3.0q fallback model (low-effort, config-only). This should recover most user-facing latency.
B) Short-term (30-180m): roll back burst pool concurrency knob (agent config) and revert to v3.0q for the production pool.
C) Medium-term (3-7 days): patch the attention kernel path for quantized matmul (low-risk perf fix) and add a guarding concurrency check.

I can run the canary rollback with infra if you give the green light. No code changes required for the 0-30m mitigation.

—Karthik
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Attachments: none (perf traces available at related_links)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin_lee@redwood.ai>
To: Sandeep Rao <sandeep@optiledger.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
Date: Fri, 14 May 2027 15:58:00 -07:00
Subject: OptiLedger incident update and next steps (v3.1q)

Sandeep —

Quick executive update and next steps after our internal triage:
- Impact: we observed a P95 latency regression and elevated 5xx rate affecting real-time pipelines, root cause tied to v3.1q quantized attention path under high concurrency (explained below).
- Immediate mitigation (complete): we routed 15% of traffic to v3.0q fallback and throttled burst-pool concurrency — observed P95 drop back to ~420–500ms in the affected flows.
- Rollback plan: if OptiLedger prefers zero-risk, we can cut back the production pool to v3.0q now; Karthik can run the rollback with infra within 30 minutes. Otherwise we propose a staged rollback: canary -> monitor -> full if metrics improve.
- Compensation proposal: if the incident window exceeds 1 hour of degraded latency for >10% of requests, we propose a credit equivalent to 25% of that hour’s invoice for the impacted routes (we can finalize language with Marissa).

Technical summary (for your engineers): the quant path in v3.1q includes more aggressive packing of attention keys and a reduced KV threshold which, combined with burst concurrent requests, pushed execution into a fallback matmul that is not yet optimized for the quantized kernel under contention. This results in the increased per-request latency and higher transient error rates.

Next action options (please confirm preference):
1) Full rollback to v3.0q now (lowest risk) — ETA 30 min.
2) Staged rollback: canary for 10% traffic, monitor 15 minutes, then full rollback if stable — ETA 45–60 min.
3) Proceed with hotfix patch to the attention path (ETA 3–6 hours to canary) and keep fallback routing in place.

Please reply with 1 / 2 / 3 and we will execute immediately. I will also prepare a post-incident report and timeline once we stabilize.

Soojin Lee
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
Soojin.Lee@redwood.ai | +1-415-555-0126
